title: Pediatric Nephrolithiasis: Cystinuria, Primary Hyperoxaluria and Citrate Management
subject: ss-paediatric-nephrology

steps.say: Underlying metabolic derangements account for the vast majority of pediatric nephrolithiasis cases.
steps.tx: Recognize the fundamental principle of **Metabolic etiology dominance in children** presenting with kidney stones. Unlike adult nephrolithiasis where dietary habits and environmental factors predominate, over 75-80% of children with urolithiasis have an identifiable underlying metabolic risk factor; idiopathic hypercalciuria represents by far the most common single metabolic abnormality, identified in 40-50% of pediatric stone formers, followed by hypocitraturia, hyperuricosuria, and cystinuria.

vis.alt: Randall plaque in the papilla initiating calcium oxalate stone growth.
vis.caption: Stones start on Randall plaque in the papilla. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Timed twenty-four-hour urine collections establish quantitative excretion benchmarks for metabolic evaluation.
steps.tx: Perform comprehensive metabolic workup using **24-hour urine collection diagnostic benchmarks** in all stone-forming children. Diagnostic criteria for urinary solute abnormalities include: hypercalciuria defined as urinary calcium > 4 mg/kg/day (or spot urine calcium-to-creatinine ratio > 0.2 mg/mg after age 2 years); hyperoxaluria defined as oxalate excretion > 0.5 mmol/1.73m²/day; hypocitraturia defined as citrate excretion < 320 mg/1.73m²/day; and hyperuricosuria defined as uric acid excretion > 10 mg/kg/day.

steps.say: Primary hyperoxaluria type one leads to aggressive nephrocalcinosis and systemic oxalosis in young infants.
steps.tx: Identify the genetic and clinical features of **Primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1) AGXT defect** in infantile nephrolithiasis. Primary hyperoxaluria type 1 is a devastating autosomal recessive inborn error of metabolism caused by mutations in the AGXT gene on chromosome 2q37.3, which encodes hepatic peroxisomal alanine:glyoxylate aminotransferase; absence of this enzyme shunts glyoxylate to oxalate, causing profound hyperoxaluria, recurrent nephrocalcinosis, early renal failure, and systemic oxalosis.

nodes.label: Glyoxylate cannot transaminate -> shunted to Oxalate

steps.say: Small interfering RNA molecules silence hepatic glycolate oxidase and provide transformative therapy for primary hyperoxaluria.
steps.tx: Prescribe disease-modifying RNA-interference therapy with **Lumasiran and nedosiran RNAi breakthrough** in pediatric PH1. Subcutaneous lumasiran is an RNA-interference therapeutic agent targeting glycolate oxidase (encoded by HAO1); by depleting glycolate oxidase, it halts upstream glyoxylate substrate synthesis, achieving a dramatic reduction in urinary oxalate excretion by > 65% in pediatric trials, preserving renal function and halting systemic calcium oxalate crystal deposition.

steps.say: Defective dibasic amino acid transport leads to precipitation of pathognomonic hexagonal crystals in acidic urine.
steps.tx: Evaluate transport genetics in **Cystinuria SLC3A1/SLC7A9 transporter defect** manifesting with recurrent calculi. Cystinuria is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in SLC3A1 (type A) or SLC7A9 (type B), which encode the heavy and light subunits of the renal and intestinal dibasic amino acid transporter responsible for reabsorbing COLA (cystine, ornithine, lysine, and arginine); insolubility of cystine in acidic urine forms radiopaque stones and pathognomonic flat hexagonal crystals.

vis.alt: Proximal tubular transporter defects in cystinuria and Fanconi syndrome.
vis.caption: Transporter defects behind cystinuria and Fanconi syndrome. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Therapy requires vigorous hydration, urinary alkalinization above pH seven point five, and thiol binding agents.
steps.tx: Formulate a comprehensive regimen for **Urinary alkalinization and tiopronin in cystinuria** stone prevention. Because cystine solubility increases exponentially above pH 7.0-7.5, medical management demands aggressive hydration exceeding 3 L/m²/day day and night, oral potassium citrate to maintain urine pH >= 7.5, and the addition of thiol-binding chelating agents (such as tiopronin or D-penicillamine) which cleave cystine disulfides into much more soluble mixed cysteine-drug complexes.

nodes.label: Aggressive fluid intake (> 3 L/m²/day around clock)
Potassium citrate to maintain urine pH >= 7.5
Add Tiopronin if cystine excretion remains > 250 mg/L

steps.say: Urinary citrate acts as a natural inhibitor of calcium crystallization and is repleted with oral potassium citrate.
steps.tx: Prescribe physiological stone inhibition using **Hypocitraturia and potassium citrate dosing** in recurrent stone formers. Citrate is a potent endogenous inhibitor of calcium stone formation that chelates free ionized calcium and directly poisons calcium oxalate and calcium phosphate crystal growth; hypocitraturia (often secondary to distal renal tubular acidosis or chronic diarrhea) is treated with oral potassium citrate (1-2 mEq/kg/day divided into 2-3 daily doses) to restore urinary citrate excretion.

left.title: Potassium Citrate Therapy
points: Alkalinizes urine and provides systemic alkali load
Complexes ionic calcium to prevent crystal nucleation

right.title: Sodium Citrate (Avoid)
points: Reserved only for patients with severe hyperkalemia

steps.say: Premature neonates treated with chronic furosemide are at high risk for medullary nephrocalcinosis.
steps.tx: Monitor high-risk infants to detect **Nephrocalcinosis in preterm infants on furosemide** during neonatal intensive care. Chronic loop diuretic therapy with furosemide in very low birth weight preterm neonates induces massive hypercalciuria, precipitating microscopic and macroscopic medullary nephrocalcinosis in up to 60% of exposed infants; management involves serial renal ultrasonography, weaning loop diuretics, and transitioning to a calcium-sparing thiazide diuretic like chlorothiazide.

vis.title: Neonatal Nephrocalcinosis Risk and Resolution
rows: Inhibits loop NKCC2, wasting calcium into urine
Transition to chlorothiazide to spare calcium
Immature tubular transport and high bone turnover
